messages:
pranav: Quick heads-up — ran the int6 candidate (rwd-v6-int6) through the small-sample synth suite this morning. small-sample=5k prompts across short/long/instruction slices. Results look mixed, posting the short summary below.

nina: thanks, pls paste the signal diffs. any latency wins?

pranav: Latency: p50 down ~12%, p95 down ~18% on T4 pool. Cost per-token estimate ~-28%.

pranav: Quality: ROUGE/Exact match roughly flat on short answers, but long-form hallucination rate up ~1.8% absolute on the longcontext slice. Safety fuzz triggered on ~0.3% more prompts.

jordan: that's the part we worry about. Where are we seeing hallucinations — topic drift, invented facts, or repetition?

pranav: Mostly invented facts and confident-sounding hallucinations on multi-step instructions; I dug into a sample of 50 failures, 70% were multi-hop reasoning.

sam: Can we run a gated A/B at 1% traffic with shadowing and explicit rerank fallback? propose: 1% production shadow for 24h -> metrics: hallucination-rate, p95 latency, top-k agreement with baseline. If hallucination delta > 1.0% abs OR agreement < 92% -> auto-fallback. Thoughts?

maria: +1 on shadow. Suggest adding a token-level confidence delta (avg log-prob difference) as a soft signal. Also add a sanity check for docs-only prompts slice.

pranav: Good call. I'll fold confidence-delta into the metric pack. Current draft gate rules (working config):
```json
{
  "target_pct": 1,
  "duration_hours": 24,
  "metrics": {
    "hallucination_abs_delta": 1.0,
    "agreement_pct": 92,
    "p95_latency_ms_delta": 40
  },
  "auto_fallback": true,
  "fallback_policy": "immediate_on_threshold",
  "monitoring_hooks": ["eval-bot/smoke-eval", "trace-ingest"]
}
```

nina: p95 delta 40ms seems small given quant wins, but ok as a latency SLO lock. How do we compute hallucination_abs_delta? binary micro-label vs baseline?
\
pranav: We use the micro-eval produced labels from the synthetic suite (human-labeled subset + heuristic detector). It's the absolute difference in % of prompts labeled as hallucination. eval-bot will publish the estimate + CI.
\
eval-bot: quick report: rwd-v6-int6 shadow run (n=5000) -> hallucination_est=4.7% (CI +/-0.5%). baseline rwd-v6-fp16 -> 2.9% (CI +/-0.4%). abs_delta ~1.8% -> exceeds proposed 1.0% threshold. Full sample list uploaded to //internal/snapshots/1745678900/int6-fail-samples.log
\
jordan: eval-bot numbers look bad. Does the increase concentrate on specific prompt archetypes?
\
pranav: yes — mostly "stepwise reasoning" and "multi-document synthesis". KV-cache warmup doesn't seem related. The int6 quant path modifies attention kernel slightly which might affect long dependency fidelity.
\
sam: Given eval-bot output, I'd pause aggressive promotion. Instead: 0.1% canary with rerank fallback + targeted mitigations (rerank by baseline or confidence throttle). Also try a hybrid quant profile: int6 on embeddings/lm-head-only vs body fp16.
\
maria: Agreed. Another experiment: run int6 but keep self-critique chain-of-thought enabled (post-process step) to see if hallucination delta shrinks. Could be calibration issue.
\
pranav: Plan: 1) Abort scheduled 10% soft-promote. 2) Launch 0.1% canary with shadow and rerank fallback + confidence gating. 3) Run hybrid-int6-body-fp16 shadow experiment. 4) Collect 48h metrics and reconvene. I'll create the rollout ticket and attach the eval artifacts.
\
nina: Thanks. Please tag me on the ticket. Also add a backup quick-rollback playbook (command snippets + runbook link).
\
pranav: Will do. Rollout ticket: #RL-3421. Quick-rollback: `redwood rollout cancel --id RL-3421 && redwood route set default rwd-v6-fp16`.
\
jordan: Good call. If hybrid reduces hallucination delta < 0.6% and agreement > 94% we can consider a staged increase.
\
sam: I'll prep the rerank fallback code; will use baseline model scoring + threshold .7 confidence. Est ETA 6h.
\
maria: Adding note: alert on CI crossing too (if CI lower bound > 1.0% then immediate alert).
\
pranav: thanks everyone. I'll post the initial canary link when it's live. :rocket:
